# #711 — core.hooksPath is absolute in .git/config, so every lane worktree runs the primary checkout's hooks

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-10T01:53:52Z
Updated: 2026-08-10T01:53:52Z

---

## What happens

`core.hooksPath` in this clone's `.git/config` is the ABSOLUTE path
`/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain/_githooks`. Because
`.git/config` is shared by every linked worktree, a lane worktree under
`{temp_workspace}/open-brain/_worktrees/` runs the PRIMARY CHECKOUT's copy of
`_githooks/pre-push` — the copy sitting on the base branch, not the one the
lane is changing.

Measured this session (lane for #709):

```
$ git config --show-origin --get core.hooksPath
file:.git/config	/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain/_githooks

$ cd <lane worktree> && git config --get core.hooksPath
/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain/_githooks
```

## Why this is a defect and not a preference

`_githooks/install.sh` already decided the opposite, in a comment written
against this exact trap:

```
# Resolve to a repo-root-relative value, not an absolute one: an absolute path
# is a clone-specific string that would be wrong in every other checkout, and
# core.hooksPath is per-repo config that only this clone reads anyway.
```

It sets `core.hooksPath=_githooks`. Git resolves a relative `core.hooksPath`
against the worktree root, so the installer's value gives each worktree its
OWN hooks. The live config does not match what the installer writes, so the
divergence happened after (or instead of) an install run. Nothing detects it:
the installer is idempotent and reports "already set" only for an exact
match, and no check asserts the value is relative.

## Consequence

`docs/lane-contract.md` round 28 named this as the third instance of one
family — a gate resolving its base or its tree from something other than the
change under review (the other two were #706 and #705). The specific bite:

- a lane fixing a git hook structurally **cannot exercise its own fix** on
  push; it exercises the base branch's copy.
- a lane whose pre-push is broken ON THE BASE BRANCH pays for it even when its
  own branch fixes it, and vice versa: a lane can break `_githooks/pre-push`
  and every local push still passes.
- proving a hook fix live requires `-c core.hooksPath=<lane worktree>/_githooks`
  by hand (what PR #708 had to do), which is a workaround a lane must know to
  reach for.

## Suggested direction (not implemented here)

1. Set `core.hooksPath` to the relative `_githooks` — i.e. what
   `_githooks/install.sh` already writes — so each worktree resolves its own.
2. Add a done-means clause asserting the configured value is RELATIVE, so an
   absolute value cannot silently return. Assert positively on the value; a
   check that merely confirms hooks ran cannot tell which tree they came from.
3. Consider having `scripts/lane-bootstrap.ts` report the effective
   `core.hooksPath` for the worktree it creates, so a lane sees which hooks it
   is about to run (AGENTS.md: nothing is adjusted silently).
